newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO PLANS TO PUT OUT UNCHANGED SIDE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO PLANS TO PUT OUT UNCHANGED SIDE.

text.p: Brazil will be unchanged against Italy in the Tournoi de France on Sunday in a repeat of the 1994 World Cup final, coach Mario Zagallo said on Wednesday.
"Provided there is no problem between now and the match it will be the same team," Zagallo said at Brazil's Chateau de Pizay retreat outside Lyon.

It was not an official announcement, but a statement of intent during an interview on a rest day for the Brazil squad after their 1-1 draw with hosts France in Tuesday's opening match of the World Cup warm-up tournament.
Zagallo said he did not like making many changes, even at experimental stages.
"I like to keep a solid base and make a few adjustments," the 65-year-old coach said.

He played down the billing of Sunday's match in Lyon as a repeat of the Los Angeles World Cup final three years ago when Carlos Parreira's Brazilians, with Zagallo as his right hand man, won their fourth title on penalties.
"That's just reliving the past," he said. "A revenge match would only be possible in the World Cup.
"It's a big match between two sides that have seven world titles between them. But Italy have the advantage of being in better shape because of the (World Cup) qualifiers."

Zagallo, questioned about players not included in his squad for the Tournoi de France and Copa America that comes right after it, said that picking the Brazil national team was a difficult task given the depth of talent in the country.
"Since 1994 I have used 100 players," he said.

The team that played against France, with two cha that which lost 4-2 to Norway in a friendly five days earlier, was: Taffarel; Cafu, Celio Silva, Aldair, Roberto Carlos; Giovanni, Mauro Silva, Dunga, Leonardo; Ronaldo, Romario.
